title: NoSQL Access Pattern Modeling Lab
description: Compare document, key-value, wide-column, and graph models using a bounded equipment-loan design with explicit indexing and consistency trade-offs.

questions.question_text: What should drive the first NoSQL modeling discussion?
options: Required reads, writes, invariants, and growth bounds
questions.explanation: Access patterns and guarantees determine whether a representation is suitable.

questions.question_text: Which model naturally groups nested fields into an aggregate?
questions.explanation: Documents can group nested related data.

questions.question_text: When is embedding a promising choice?
options: The array grows forever without bounds
Every field changes independently across millions of copies
Related data is bounded and usually read together
No query uses the embedded data
questions.explanation: Aggregate ownership and bounded access support embedding.

questions.question_text: What risk comes from embedding unlimited loan history?
options: Unbounded aggregate growth and update cost
questions.explanation: Growing arrays need explicit bounds or another access path.

questions.question_text: What is the simplest key value access pattern?
options: Lookup a value by a known key
questions.explanation: The abstract model centers on direct key lookup.

questions.question_text: A borrower cache entry is missing. What can be concluded?
options: The borrower certainly has no loans
The cache lacks a value, not that the borrower has no loans
questions.explanation: Cache absence and domain absence are different.

questions.question_text: What does time to live alone fail to guarantee?
options: Immediate invalidation after every source change
questions.explanation: TTL is not instantaneous synchronization with the source.

questions.question_text: What is a partition key responsible for in a typical wide column design?
options: Grouping records into a placement and access unit
questions.explanation: Partition choice affects grouping and operational distribution.

questions.question_text: Why is one constant partition key risky for all campus loans?
options: It ensures each borrower has an independent partition
questions.explanation: A constant key can create a hot unbounded partition.

questions.question_text: What trade off can time bucketing introduce?
options: No storage cost and no query changes
Bounded partitions but queries across multiple buckets
Removal of all secondary access paths
questions.explanation: Bounding partitions can require explicit bucket enumeration.

questions.question_text: What does a property graph emphasize?
options: Only opaque values by integer key
questions.explanation: The graph model makes connected entities and paths explicit.

questions.question_text: Does drawing BORROWED edges alone enforce one active borrower per item?
options: Yes, every graph forbids multiple edges
No, constraints and transaction logic still matter
questions.explanation: A relationship representation does not automatically enforce exclusivity.

questions.question_text: Why bound graph traversal length?
options: To guarantee every path is unique
To control the explored path space and cost
questions.explanation: Unbounded exploration can expand rapidly in connected data.

questions.question_text: What does an additional index usually require?
options: A separate physical server per row
questions.explanation: Indexes trade maintenance resources for useful access paths.

questions.question_text: Does NoSQL necessarily mean eventual consistency?
questions.explanation: Consistency and atomicity guarantees must be checked per engine and operation.

questions.question_text: Which data might tolerate weaker freshness than an exclusive checkout decision?
questions.explanation: Read contracts depend on the consequence of stale data.

questions.question_text: What obligation does deliberate denormalization create?
questions.explanation: Copies need authoritative ownership and propagation or repair rules.

questions.question_text: What is useful for safely repeated projection processing?
options: Suitable event identity or version checks
Assuming every message arrives exactly once
Using a new source identity for each retry
questions.explanation: Identity and versions can help detect repeats and stale updates.

questions.question_text: A department is reached through two borrowed items. What decides duplicate output?
options: Whether the query asks for paths or distinct departments
questions.explanation: Result grain determines whether repeated paths should be collapsed.

questions.question_text: What should a derived view rebuild plan identify?
options: Authoritative source, rebuild procedure, and interim behavior
Only the count of JSON braces
questions.explanation: A rebuildable projection still needs an operational recovery contract.

notes:
## Choose a model from the required reads and writes

NoSQL describes a broad family of database approaches rather than one storage engine or one consistency guarantee. Document, key value, wide column, and graph systems organize access differently. Some products support multiple models. The useful design question is not whether data can be drawn as JSON, but which operations must be efficient, which facts must change together, and which consistency rules the application needs. Start with a bounded example and explicit access patterns before selecting a model.

Imagine a campus equipment service. Users view one borrower's active loans, search equipment by category, and trace which department owns an item. Borrowing must not give the same physical item to two people at once. A borrower dashboard and an ownership traversal are different access patterns. A model that makes one easy may require another index, a duplicated projection, or a separate query path for the other. Write these trade offs down before deciding that one representation solves the whole service.

## Document databases

A document groups named fields and nested structures into an aggregate. A borrower document could contain a small array of active loan summaries. Reading one borrower then retrieves the dashboard without joining separate records. The document boundary can also define an atomic update scope, depending on the engine. MongoDB supports atomic writes to a single document and also supports multi document transactions with their own documented requirements and costs. Do not simplify that into either unlimited automatic atomicity or an assertion that transactions never exist.

```json
{
  "borrower_id": "B17",
  "display_name": "Mira",
  "active_loans": [
    {"item_id": "CAM4", "due_day": "2026-11-02"},
    {"item_id": "MIC2", "due_day": "2026-11-05"}
  ]
}
```

Embedding works well when related data is read together, bounded, and owned by the same aggregate. An ever growing loan history array can become too large or costly to update, and a shared equipment description copied into thousands of borrowers creates update fanout. Referencing a separate item document avoids some duplication but requires additional reads or supported join mechanisms. Distinguish a current reference from an intentional historical snapshot, such as the equipment description printed on a completed loan receipt.

## Key value stores

A key value model retrieves a value by a known key. For example, borrower: B17: dashboard can map to a serialized dashboard. The application often controls the value's internal interpretation. This is useful when the dominant operation is direct lookup, but it does not automatically support arbitrary filtering inside values. Product capabilities vary: some key value systems add structures, indexes, transactions, or scripting. Verify the selected engine rather than defining all products by the simplest abstract model.

A cached dashboard illustrates an important boundary. If it is derived from authoritative loans, its expiration and invalidation policy determine freshness. A missing cache entry must not mean that a borrower has no loans, and a stale dashboard must not authorize a second checkout of an already borrowed item. Cache reads and authoritative business decisions require different contracts. Time to live limits persistence under a policy; it is not proof that every change instantly invalidates every copy.

## Wide column models

Wide column systems commonly organize rows by partition keys and order records within a partition using clustering components. Exact terminology and capabilities differ by product. An access pattern for loans by borrower could use borrower_id as a partition key and checkout_time plus loan_id for ordering. A query for equipment maintenance by item would need a different access path. Designing these tables around queries can deliberately duplicate information to make bounded reads efficient.

Partition sizing matters. Putting every campus loan under one constant partition key creates concentrated load and potentially unbounded growth. A borrower with unusually many events can also become a hot partition. Adding a time bucket can bound partitions but means a crossbucket query must enumerate the relevant buckets. This is a measurable trade off between write distribution and read complexity. A partition key is therefore an operational choice as well as a logical grouping label.

## Graph databases

A property graph represents entities as nodes and connections as typed relationships, with properties on either. Borrower B17 can have a BORROWED relationship to item CAM4; CAM4 can have an OWNED_BY relationship to department MEDIA. This representation supports traversing connections such as the departments associated with items borrowed by one person. It is especially useful when the relationship paths themselves are central to the questions, rather than when every workload is a lookup of one independent record.

Graph modeling still needs cardinality, identity, constraints, and transaction analysis. A relationship does not automatically enforce that an item has only one active borrower. Path expansion can also become expensive when a query explores many highly connected nodes without bounds. Specify direction, relationship type, path length, and duplicate handling. Drawing a visually appealing network is not evidence that the actual traversal has a suitable cost or that the booking invariant is protected.

## Indexing and consistency are separate decisions

An index is an access path supporting particular predicates or ordering. A document database can index borrower identifiers and due dates, while a key value abstraction may require constructing an explicit secondary lookup. Extra indexes consume storage and add write work. Indexing every field is not a substitute for knowing the queries. For a borrower dashboard, identify the equality condition, requested sort, result limit, and maximum expected active loan count before evaluating an index.

Do not equate NoSQL with eventual consistency. Products and operations offer different consistency levels and transaction scopes. A stale equipment description might be acceptable for browsing; a stale active borrower flag may be unacceptable for granting checkout. Define the visibility and atomicity required for each action. A replicated model must also describe what happens during a partition, how conflicting writes are handled, and whether a successful response represents an authoritative business outcome.

Denormalization shifts maintenance obligations into writes or projection pipelines. If the same item category appears in three read models, decide which record owns it and how changes propagate. A repair job needs a way to find divergence, not merely an assumption that all messages arrive once and in order. Derived views can be rebuilt when their source is retained, but rebuilding time and interim stale behavior still matter. Record versions or event identities when they support safe repeated processing.

## Three solved modeling exercises

Exercise one: borrowers have at most five active loans, the dashboard reads all five together, and loan history grows indefinitely. What should be embedded? A bounded active summary can be a reasonable document choice, while history should have a separate bounded access path. The exact source of truth for item availability must still be defined. The bounded dashboard alone cannot prove exclusive checkout across borrower aggregates.

Exercise two: a proposed wide column table places every loan in partition campus and clusters by time. What is the concern? One partition receives all writes and grows without a natural bound. Consider a partition key aligned with the required read, such as borrower and a suitable time bucket, then account for multi bucket queries. Do not add random distribution without explaining how the application will locate the records it needs.

Exercise three: a graph query finds departments through borrowed items, but the same department is reached through two items. Should the output list it twice? The requirement must say whether it asks for paths or distinct departments. A distinct entity report should remove duplicates deliberately, while a path analysis may retain both. This is the same reasoning discipline used for joins and duplicate rows in SQL.

Before adopting a representation, document two main reads, one critical write, growth bounds, failure cases, and rebuild strategy. Compare it against a relational baseline rather than assuming a model category guarantees scale. Use [3NF](/learning/dbms-sql-tutorial/3nf) to understand the facts denormalization may duplicate and [concurrent execution](/learning/dbms-sql-tutorial/concurrent-execution) to evaluate exclusive checkout under competing requests.
